import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.68

by John S. Wilson

Let $\mathfrak V$ be a variety of groups other than the variety of all groups,
and let $p$ be a prime. Are the $p$-lengths of the finite $p$-soluble groups
whose Sylow $p$-subgroups belong to $\mathfrak V$ bounded?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.68»

/-- A variety of groups, represented by a set of group laws $w=1$ in
countably many variables. By Birkhoff's theorem, these are exactly the classes
of groups closed under subgroups, quotients, and arbitrary direct products. -/
structure GroupVariety where
  /-- The defining group laws. -/
  laws : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)

namespace GroupVariety

/-- A group belongs to a variety when it satisfies every defining law under
every substitution for the variables. -/
def Contains (V : GroupVariety) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ V.laws, ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1

/-- A group variety is proper when it is not the variety of all groups. -/
def IsProper (V : GroupVariety) : Prop :=
  ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), ¬V.Contains G

end GroupVariety

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- The order of the factor $K/H$, computed as $|K|/|H|$.
This definition is used only when $H \le K$ in a finite group. -/
noncomputable def factorOrder (H K : Subgroup G) : ℕ :=
  Nat.card K / Nat.card H

/-- A normal $p$-series from $1$ to $G$: every term is normal in $G$, and
every factor has either $p$-power order or order coprime to $p$. -/
structure NormalPSeries (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] where
  /-- The number of factors in the series. -/
  length : ℕ
  /-- The subgroups in the series. -/
  subgroup : Fin (length + 1) → Subgroup G
  head : subgroup 0 = ⊥
  last : subgroup (Fin.last length) = ⊤
  monotone : Monotone subgroup
  normal : ∀ i, (subgroup i).Normal
  factor : ∀ i : Fin length,
    (∃ a : ℕ, factorOrder (subgroup i.castSucc) (subgroup i.succ) = p ^ a) ∨
      ¬p ∣ factorOrder (subgroup i.castSucc) (subgroup i.succ)

/-- The number of nontrivial $p$-factors in a normal $p$-series. -/
noncomputable def NormalPSeries.pFactorCount {p : ℕ} (s : NormalPSeries p G) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.filter fun i : Fin s.length ↦
    p ∣ factorOrder (s.subgroup i.castSucc) (s.subgroup i.succ)).card

/-- A group is $p$-soluble if it has a normal series whose factors are
$p$-groups or $p'$-groups. -/
def IsPSoluble (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  Nonempty (NormalPSeries p G)

/-- The $p$-length of a $p$-soluble group is the least number of nontrivial
$p$-factors in a normal $p$-series. Equivalently, this is the number of
nontrivial $p$-factors in its upper $p$-series. -/
noncomputable def pLength (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : ℕ :=
  sInf {n : ℕ | ∃ s : NormalPSeries p G, s.pFactorCount = n}

/--
Let $\mathfrak V$ be a variety of groups which is not the variety of all
groups, and let $p$ be a prime. Is there a bound, depending on
$\mathfrak V$ and $p$, on the $p$-lengths of all finite $p$-soluble groups
whose Sylow $p$-subgroups belong to $\mathfrak V$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.68» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (V : GroupVariety), V.IsProper → ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime →
      ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G],
        IsPSoluble p G → (∀ P : Sylow p G, V.Contains P) → pLength p G ≤ N := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.68»
modeling_decisions: Represented a group variety by a set of identities w = 1 in the free group on countably many variables. Membership requires every identity to hold under every substitution. This is the law-based characterization equivalent, by Birkhoff's theorem, to closure under subgroups, quotients, and arbitrary direct products.
Defined properness semantically by the existence of a group outside the variety, rather than syntactically by requiring a nonempty set of laws.

Defined p-solubility using a normal series whose factors have p-power order or order not divisible by p. Defined p-length as the least number of nontrivial p-factors among such series, the standard characterization equivalent to counting nontrivial p-factors in the upper p-series.
Required all Sylow p-subgroups to belong to the variety. Since Sylow subgroups are conjugate and varieties are isomorphism-closed, this agrees with the usual phrasing.
Placed the bound after the variety and prime quantifiers and before the finite group quantifier, allowing it to depend exactly on the variety and p.

/-- A group satisfies a set of group laws if every word in the set evaluates to the identity
under every assignment of its countably many variables. -/
def SatisfiesGroupLaws (laws : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ laws, ∀ x : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift x w = 1

/-- A set of group laws defines a proper variety when not every group satisfies it. It is enough
to test this on the free group on countably many generators. -/
def DefinesProperVariety (laws : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) : Prop :=
  ¬SatisfiesGroupLaws laws (FreeGroup ℕ)

/-- A finite group has $p$-length at most $N$ if it has an ascending normal series whose factors
are $p$-groups or $p'$-groups and which has at most $N$ nontrivial $p$-group factors. Factor
orders are expressed as relative indices of consecutive terms. -/
def HasPLengthAtMost (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] (p N : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (H : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G),
    H 0 = ⊥ ∧ H (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧ Monotone H ∧
    (∀ i, (H i).Normal) ∧
    (∀ i : Fin n,
      (∃ k : ℕ, (H i.castSucc).relIndex (H i.succ) = p ^ k) ∨
        ¬p ∣ (H i.castSucc).relIndex (H i.succ)) ∧
    Nat.card {i : Fin n // p ∣ (H i.castSucc).relIndex (H i.succ)} ≤ N

/-- A group is $p$-soluble if it has a normal series whose factors are $p$-groups or
$p'$-groups. -/
def IsPSoluble (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] (p : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ N : ℕ, HasPLengthAtMost G p N

/--
Let $\mathfrak V$ be a variety of groups other than the variety of all groups, and let $p$ be a
prime. Is there a bound, depending on $\mathfrak V$ and $p$, on the $p$-lengths of all finite
$p$-soluble groups whose Sylow $p$-subgroups belong to $\mathfrak V$?

Here a variety is represented by a set of group laws. Its members are exactly the groups satisfying
all those laws.
-/

    ∀ (laws : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (p : ℕ), DefinesProperVariety laws → p.Prime →
      ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G],
        IsPSoluble G p → (∀ P : Sylow p G, SatisfiesGroupLaws laws P) →
          HasPLengthAtMost G p N := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.68»

Defined properness by failure of the laws in the countably generated free group. This is equivalent to the resulting variety not being the variety of all groups: a nonidentity word is refuted by assigning the free generators to themselves.

Used the standard equivalent normal-series characterization of p-length: p-length at most N means there is an ascending normal series with p-group or p'-group factors and at most N nontrivial p-group factors. For finite groups, relative indices give the orders of consecutive quotient factors.
Quantified the bound N after both the law set and p, so the bound may depend on the variety and the prime, but before the finite group G.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.68

by John S. Wilson

Let $\mathfrak{V}$ be a variety of groups which is not the variety of all groups, and let $p$
be a prime. Is there a bound on the $p$-lengths of the finite $p$-soluble groups whose Sylow
$p$-subgroups are in $\mathfrak{V}$?

A *variety of groups* is a class of groups closed under taking subgroups, homomorphic images and
arbitrary cartesian (direct) products; by Birkhoff's theorem these are exactly the classes of
groups defined by a set of laws.

A finite group $G$ is *$p$-soluble* if it has a normal series each of whose factors is a
$p$-group or a $p'$-group. The *$p$-length* $l_p(G)$ of a finite $p$-soluble group $G$ is the
number of $p$-factors of its upper $p$-series
$1 = P_0 \le N_0 < P_1 < N_1 < \dots < P_l \le N_l = G$, where
$N_i / P_i = O_{p'}(G / P_i)$ and $P_{i+1} / N_i = O_p(G / N_i)$ (Hall–Higman). Equivalently,
$l_p(G)$ is the least $l$ such that $G$ has a normal series
$1 = P_0 \le N_0 \le P_1 \le N_1 \le \dots \le P_l \le N_l = G$
in which every $N_i / P_i$ is a $p'$-group and every $P_{i+1} / N_i$ is a $p$-group: the upper
$p$-series is such a series, and it dominates any such series term by term. The formalisation
below uses this second description.

*References:*
* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 9.68
* P. Hall, G. Higman, *On the p-length of p-soluble groups and reduction theorems for
  Burnside's problem*, Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) 6 (1956), 1–42.
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.68»

universe u

/--
A *variety of groups* is a class of groups `𝔙` (a predicate on groups in `Type u`) that is
closed under taking subgroups, homomorphic images and arbitrary cartesian (direct) products.
Closure under subgroups and homomorphic images is stated through injective and surjective
homomorphisms, so `𝔙` is in particular closed under isomorphism. Taking the empty product shows
that the trivial group always belongs to `𝔙`.
-/
structure IsGroupVariety (𝔙 : (G : Type u) → [Group G] → Prop) : Prop where
  /-- `𝔙` is closed under taking subgroups. -/
  of_injective : ∀ {G H : Type u} [Group G] [Group H] (f : H →* G),
    Function.Injective f → 𝔙 G → 𝔙 H
  /-- `𝔙` is closed under taking homomorphic images. -/
  of_surjective : ∀ {G H : Type u} [Group G] [Group H] (f : G →* H),
    Function.Surjective f → 𝔙 G → 𝔙 H
  /-- `𝔙` is closed under arbitrary cartesian (direct) products. -/
  pi : ∀ {ι : Type u} {f : ι → Type u} [∀ i, Group (f i)],
    (∀ i, 𝔙 (f i)) → 𝔙 (∀ i, f i)

/-- The class of abelian groups is a variety of groups. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isGroupVariety_comm : IsGroupVariety.{u} (fun G _ => ∀ a b : G, a * b = b * a) where
  of_injective f hf h a b := hf (by rw [map_mul, map_mul, h])
  of_surjective f hf h a b := by
    obtain ⟨a, rfl⟩ := hf a
    obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ := hf b
    rw [← map_mul, ← map_mul, h]
  pi h a b := funext fun i => h i (a i) (b i)

variable (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G]

/--
`IsPSeries p G l P N` says that
$1 = P_0 \le N_0 \le P_1 \le N_1 \le \dots \le P_l \le N_l = G$
is a normal series of the finite group `G` (all terms `P i`, `N i` for `i ≤ l` are normal
subgroups of `G`) in which every factor $N_i / P_i$ is a $p'$-group and every factor
$P_{i+1} / N_i$ is a $p$-group. Such a series has (at most) `l` nontrivial $p$-factors.

Since `P i ≤ N i`, the order of the factor group $N_i / P_i$ is `(P i).relIndex (N i)`, and
similarly for $P_{i+1} / N_i$; so a factor is a $p'$-group iff its order is coprime to `p`
and a $p$-group iff its order is a power of `p`.
-/
structure IsPSeries (l : ℕ) (P N : ℕ → Subgroup G) : Prop where
  normal_P : ∀ i ≤ l, (P i).Normal
  normal_N : ∀ i ≤ l, (N i).Normal
  P_zero : P 0 = ⊥
  N_last : N l = ⊤
  P_le_N : ∀ i ≤ l, P i ≤ N i
  N_le_P : ∀ i < l, N i ≤ P (i + 1)
  /-- Every factor $N_i / P_i$ is a $p'$-group. -/
  coprime : ∀ i ≤ l, Nat.Coprime p ((P i).relIndex (N i))
  /-- Every factor $P_{i+1} / N_i$ is a $p$-group. -/
  pow : ∀ i < l, ∃ k : ℕ, (N i).relIndex (P (i + 1)) = p ^ k

/--
A finite group `G` is *`p`-soluble* if it has a normal series each of whose factors is a
`p`-group or a `p'`-group, i.e. a series as in `IsPSeries` for some `l`.
-/
def IsPSolvable : Prop :=
  ∃ (l : ℕ) (P N : ℕ → Subgroup G), IsPSeries p G l P N

/--
The *`p`-length* $l_p(G)$ of a finite `p`-soluble group `G`: the least `l` such that `G` has a
normal series $1 = P_0 \le N_0 \le \dots \le P_l \le N_l = G$ with all $N_i / P_i$
$p'$-groups and all $P_{i+1} / N_i$ $p$-groups. This is the number of $p$-factors of the upper
$p$-series of `G` (Hall–Higman). For a group which is not `p`-soluble the set is empty and the
value is the junk value `0`.
-/
noncomputable def pLength : ℕ :=
  sInf {l : ℕ | ∃ P N : ℕ → Subgroup G, IsPSeries p G l P N}

/-- A finite `p`-group `G` has the `p`-series `1 = P₀ = N₀ ≤ P₁ = N₁ = G`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isPSeries_of_isPGroup [Fact p.Prime] [Finite G] (hG : IsPGroup p G) :
    IsPSeries p G 1 (fun i => if i = 0 then ⊥ else ⊤)
      (fun i => if i = 0 then ⊥ else ⊤) where
  normal_P i _ := by split_ifs <;> infer_instance
  normal_N i _ := by split_ifs <;> infer_instance
  P_zero := if_pos rfl
  N_last := if_neg one_ne_zero
  P_le_N _ _ := le_rfl
  N_le_P i hi := by
    obtain rfl : i = 0 := Nat.lt_one_iff.mp hi
    simp
  coprime i _ := by simp
  pow i hi := by
    obtain rfl : i = 0 := Nat.lt_one_iff.mp hi
    simpa [Subgroup.relIndex_bot_left] using (IsPGroup.iff_card.mp hG)

/-- A finite `p`-group is `p`-soluble. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isPSolvable_of_isPGroup [Fact p.Prime] [Finite G] (hG : IsPGroup p G) :
    IsPSolvable p G :=
  ⟨_, _, _, isPSeries_of_isPGroup p G hG⟩

/-- A finite `p`-group has `p`-length at most `1`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem pLength_le_one_of_isPGroup [Fact p.Prime] [Finite G] (hG : IsPGroup p G) :
    pLength p G ≤ 1 :=
  Nat.sInf_le ⟨_, _, isPSeries_of_isPGroup p G hG⟩

/-- A finite `p'`-group has `p`-length `0`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem pLength_eq_zero_of_coprime (h : Nat.Coprime p (Nat.card G)) : pLength p G = 0 := by
  refine Nat.sInf_eq_zero.mpr (Or.inl ⟨fun _ => ⊥, fun _ => ⊤, ?_⟩)
  exact
    { normal_P := fun _ _ => inferInstance
      normal_N := fun _ _ => inferInstance
      P_zero := rfl
      N_last := rfl
      P_le_N := fun _ _ => bot_le
      N_le_P := fun i hi => absurd hi (Nat.not_lt_zero i)
      coprime := fun _ _ => by simpa [Subgroup.relIndex_bot_left] using h
      pow := fun i hi => absurd hi (Nat.not_lt_zero i) }

be a prime. Is there a bound on the $p$-lengths of the finite $p$-soluble groups whose Sylow
$p$-subgroups are in $\mathfrak{V}$?

      ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime →

/-- A variety of groups, presented by the group laws defining it. A law is a word in
countably many variables which is required to evaluate to the identity. -/
abbrev GroupVariety := Set (FreeGroup ℕ)

/-- A group belongs to the variety defined by `V` if it satisfies every law in `V`. -/
def GroupVariety.Contains (V : GroupVariety) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ V, ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1

/-- A variety is proper if one of its defining laws is nontrivial. Equivalently, it is not the
variety of all groups. -/
def GroupVariety.IsProper (V : GroupVariety) : Prop :=
  ∃ w ∈ V, w ≠ 1

/-- A normal series witnessing $p$-solubility. Each factor is labelled either as a nontrivial
$p$-group factor or as a $p'$-group factor. -/
structure PSeries (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] where
  /-- The number of factors in the series. -/
  length : ℕ
  /-- The terms of the series. -/
  subgroup : Fin (length + 1) → Subgroup G
  /-- Every term is normal in the whole group. -/
  normal : ∀ i, (subgroup i).Normal
  /-- The series starts at the trivial subgroup. -/
  bot : subgroup 0 = ⊥
  /-- The series ends at the whole group. -/
  top : subgroup (Fin.last length) = ⊤

  mono : ∀ i : Fin length, subgroup i.castSucc ≤ subgroup i.succ
  /-- `true` labels the nontrivial $p$-group factors. -/

  /-- The order of each factor is either a positive power of $p$, or is prime to $p$, according

      ∃ e > 0, Nat.card (subgroup i.succ) / Nat.card (subgroup i.castSucc) = p ^ e

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.68

by John S. Wilson

Let $\mathfrak V$ be a proper variety of groups and let $p$ be a prime. Is there a
bound on the $p$-lengths of the finite $p$-soluble groups whose Sylow $p$-subgroups
belong to $\mathfrak V$?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.68»

/-- A group law is a word in finitely many formal generators, required to equal $1$. -/
abbrev GroupLaw := Σ n : ℕ, FreeGroup (Fin n)

/-- A group satisfies a law if the word evaluates to $1$ under every assignment of its
formal generators. -/
def GroupLaw.IsSatisfiedBy (law : GroupLaw) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ f : Fin law.1 → G, FreeGroup.lift f law.2 = 1

/-- A variety of groups, presented by a set of group laws. Membership means satisfaction
of all the laws in the presentation. -/
structure GroupVariety where
  laws : Set GroupLaw

/-- A group belongs to a variety when it satisfies every defining law. -/
def GroupVariety.Contains (V : GroupVariety) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ law ∈ V.laws, law.IsSatisfiedBy G

/-- A law-presented variety is proper if its defining laws include a nonidentity word. -/
def GroupVariety.IsProper (V : GroupVariety) : Prop :=
  ∃ law ∈ V.laws, law.2 ≠ 1

/-- The order of the factor $B/A$ in a finite group. -/
noncomputable def factorOrder {G : Type*} [Group G] (A B : Subgroup G) : ℕ :=
  Nat.card B / Nat.card A

/-- A normal $p$-series is a chain whose successive factors are either $p$-groups or
$p'$-groups. Normality here is normality of each subgroup in the next subgroup. -/
def IsPSeries {G : Type*} [Group G] (p : ℕ) : List (Subgroup G) → Prop
  | [] => True
  | [_] => True
  | A :: B :: tail =>
      A ≤ B ∧ (A.subgroupOf B).Normal ∧
        ((∃ k : ℕ, factorOrder A B = p ^ k) ∨ (factorOrder A B).Coprime p) ∧
        IsPSeries p (B :: tail)
termination_by series => series.length

/-- The number of nontrivial $p$-factors in a normal $p$-series. -/
noncomputable def pFactorCount {G : Type*} [Group G] (p : ℕ) : List (Subgroup G) → ℕ
  | A :: B :: tail =>
      (if p ∣ factorOrder A B then 1 else 0) + pFactorCount p (B :: tail)
  | _ => 0
termination_by series => series.length

/-- A group has $p$-length at most `n` if it has a normal $p$-series from the trivial
subgroup to the whole group with at most `n` nontrivial $p$-factors. For finite
$p$-soluble groups this is equivalent to counting the nontrivial $p$-factors in the
upper $p$-series. -/
def HasPLengthAtMost (p n : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ series : List (Subgroup G),
    series.head? = some ⊥ ∧ series.getLast? = some ⊤ ∧
      IsPSeries p series ∧ pFactorCount p series ≤ n

/-- A group is $p$-soluble if it has a finite normal $p$-series. -/
def IsPSoluble (p : ℕ) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, HasPLengthAtMost p n G

/--
Let $\mathfrak V$ be a variety of groups other than the variety of all groups, and
let $p$ be prime. Is there a bound $N$, depending on $\mathfrak V$ and $p$, such that
every finite $p$-soluble group whose Sylow $p$-subgroups belong to $\mathfrak V$ has
$p$-length at most $N$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.68» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (V : GroupVariety) (p : ℕ), V.IsProper → p.Prime →
      ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G],
        IsPSoluble p G → (∀ P : Sylow p G, V.Contains P) → HasPLengthAtMost p N G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.68»
modeling_decisions: Represented a variety by a set of group identities, each a word in finitely many free generators required to evaluate to 1. This is the equational presentation equivalent to closure under subgroups, quotients, and arbitrary direct products.

Defined properness by the presence of a nonidentity free-group word among the defining laws. Such a word fails in the corresponding free group, while presentations containing only identity words define the variety of all groups.

Expressed p-length at most N using the standard equivalent characterization by a finite normal p-series from the trivial subgroup to the whole group, counting its nontrivial p-factors. For finite p-soluble groups, the minimum such count equals the number of nontrivial p-factors in the upper p-series.
Used `Finite G` for the source's finite groups and Mathlib's `Sylow p G`; membership in the variety is required for every Sylow p-subgroup.
Placed the existential bound after the universally quantified variety and prime, so it may depend on both, and before the universally quantified finite group.
